It addresses the problem where saturated regions (over- or undersaturation) lack reliable texture cues, acting as outliers that bias geometric and photometric recovery.
It sets itself apart from standard masking by using a "leaky" quadratic transition rather than a hard binary cutoff, allowing for smoother gradient flow at the boundaries of saturation.
The method computes a scalar mask value for each pixel based on its intensity, which modulates the contribution of that pixel to the training loss.
